result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same main causes of the generic look and both name the ampersand or crumb as a direction that fits the name. B has the sharper point that a playful name doesn't suit a heritage-script style. A is better on what to keep: it says to keep the dark brown and the script if customers already recognize them and to strip everything else. It also gives more practical tests at small size and in one color, and ends with a clearer next step. B suggests replacing the palette and the script outright, so it says little about what to keep. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the specific clichés behind the generic look and flag what fails at small sizes. B is better on what to keep: it treats the dark brown script as recognition worth preserving and frames a refine-or-replace choice, while A mostly throws the logo out, even the color. B also gives more concrete small-size tests (solid black at 32px, reversed on dark) and ends with a clearer next step.
